title: Recruitment scams have turned J&K’s job aspirants into victims: Mehbooba Mufti

ai.summary: Mehbooba Mufti, PDP president, demanded postponement of Jammu and Kashmir police sub-inspector recruitment exams due to alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, claiming youth are being targeted and exploitation of the recruitment process.

facts.claim: Mehbooba Mufti demanded postponement of police sub-inspector recruitment examination scheduled for November 28
facts.quote: Mehbooba Mufti on Monday called for a transparent investigation into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jammu and Kashmir and demanded postponement of the police sub-inspector recruitment examination scheduled for November 28.

facts.claim: Mehbooba Mufti said youth are being targeted and their interests not given priority
facts.quote: It seems that in Jammu and Kashmir, the youth are not the priority; rather, they are the target,

facts.claim: Mehbooba Mufti referred to alleged irregularities in the recent Financial Accounts Assistants (FAA) recruitment examination conducted by the Jammu and Kashmir Services Selection Board (JKSSB)
facts.quote: Referring to allegations of irregularities in the recent Financial Accounts Assistants (FAA) recruitment examination conducted by the Jammu and Kashmir Services Selection Board (JKSSB)

facts.claim: Mehbooba Mufti claimed that papers get leaked and authorities round up low-level employees or daily-wage workers
facts.quote: Despite this, papers get leaked, and in response, the authorities merely round up low-level employees or daily-wage workers,

facts.claim: Mehbooba Mufti questioned Chief Minister Omar Abdullah's position
facts.quote: But now he claims nothing is in his hands,

facts.claim: Mehbooba Mufti said young aspirants were protesting on the streets
facts.quote: She said young aspirants were protesting on the streets, distressed by what she described as exploitation and the loss of faith in the recruitment process.

ai.background_note: Mehbooba Mufti, PDP president, is demanding a transparent investigation into alleged irregularities in Jammu and Kashmir's recruitment examinations, specifically targeting the police sub-inspector recruitment exam scheduled for November 28, which she claims is being conducted without proper oversight.
